complexity: High: this combines entry-point/tool semantics, UI accessibility and command discoverability, an undocumented changing API, untrusted metadata/media URLs, external media resolution, playback-mode state, CSP/network policy, autoplay gesture rules, and cross-thread browser coordination.
evidence: Current server exposes open_radio with one known Radio Paradise station and find_stations_by_country with a country resource; current country resource includes NTS 1/2 as a tab, so there is no dedicated NTS app entry point or archive-search tool yet.

Current NTS direct live URLs are stream-relay-geo.ntslive.net/stream and /stream2 with client=direct; current policy lists the relay and two redirect origins observed on 2026-11-12. This is existing tested live-channel policy, not evidence for archive media origins.

PlaybackCoordinator.pauseRemote() sends a bounded pause request to a reported active peer, waits up to 1800 ms for acknowledgement, and reports failure when no peer is available. Coordination is via Web Locks and BroadcastChannel; these are browser-context capabilities and provide no cross-device identity or guarantee.

The reference describes NTS archive API as undocumented, derived from nts.live player calls. It requires version=2 for useful /search results, clamps query to 120 characters and page size to 1..40, and parses show/episode results from /api/v2/search.

Bounded live NTS response check on 2026-11-13: GET https://www.nts.live/api/v2/search?q=Floating%20Points&version=2&offset=0&limit=3&types%5B%5D=show returned HTTP JSON with result count 13 and three show metadata rows. A separate limit=6 episode query returned count 639 and six episode metadata rows; sampled audio_sources pointed to soundcloud.com. No complete inventory was requested or retained.
Reference NtsApi.js accepts episode audio source pages only on HTTPS SoundCloud/Mixcloud hosts and warns against shipping NTS's embedded Basic credential for /resolve-stream.

Reference README says NTS does not host archive audio: episode sources are SoundCloud or Mixcloud; local playback relies on mpv yt-dlp hook. Resolver.qml uses yt-dlp to select progressive HTTP(S) and describes HLS/DASH as unsuitable for its Chromecast direct-media path. Dial's browser app cannot run this local subprocess.
The reference preserves archive seek/resume position but treats live resume as rejoining the current relay; carrying these semantics to browser media needs an explicit Spec and host verification.

Public NTS episode page evidence and NTS Supporter copy expose archive episodes and state that tracklist timestamps are a supporter feature; do not expose timestamps as generally available. Sources: https://www.nts.live/shows/selassie-tbc/episodes/selassie-tbc-8th-may-2020 and https://www.nts.live/supporters.

Browser-host playback evidence remains distinct from metadata response: the bounded API response proves metadata discovery only. No browser media request, redirect/CSP outcome, audible playback, or archive seek/pause behavior was tested in ChatGPT host.
open_questions: Should NTS archive playback be limited to an NTS-hosted/site playback surface or external SoundCloud/Mixcloud link when safe direct in-app media resolution is unavailable? No browser-compatible archive resolver is established by current code or the native reference.
What are the exact approved NTS API request, timeout, query/page/response caps, metadata fields, and fallback behavior if the undocumented endpoint changes or returns no results?

What archive playback formats/origins, expiring URL handling, CSP resourceDomains, and failure states can be verified in the actual ChatGPT host, separately from API metadata and protocol reachability?

Should the product provide separate open_country_radio and open_nts_radio entry-point tools, plus a discoverable help/command tool (for example dial_help) and pause_dial command? Define exact invocation wording and how a pause command opens/targets a same-browser player when no active app is mounted in that thread.
Which accessible command/help presentation is preferred (tool descriptions, in-app prompt list, help action, or combination), and what keyboard/screen-reader acceptance checks are required?
Does the owner require NTS archive seek, resume-from-position, and replay semantics to match the native reference, and what behavior should apply when the media provider does not support seeking?
How should the UI disclose that NTS search metadata is from an unofficial, undocumented endpoint and that audible playback depends on browser host/network support?

risks: Treating API search success or an audio_sources URL as proof that archived audio can play in an MCP App would overstate evidence; source pages are not direct audio streams.

Unbounded archive scraping, arbitrary URL resolution, importing an NTS embedded credential, or creating an undocumented proxy would add trust, privacy, and operational risk; keep any proposed query/page/response sizes bounded and constrain origins.
SoundCloud/Mixcloud resolved media may use expiring signed URLs and progressive/HLS/DASH variants; do not persist or share resolved URLs. Exact browser-host behavior needs evidence.
Autoplay may be blocked. Playback must begin only from an explicit user gesture in the app, with a clear Play action and failure state.
Cross-thread controls can only be described within the tested same-browser/profile/device context where Web Locks/BroadcastChannel are shared; do not imply synchronization across browsers or devices.
Separate country and NTS entry points could duplicate playback owners. They should reuse the existing coordinator and maintain a single active player/ownership contract.
scope: Triage of separate country-radio and NTS entry points, bounded NTS archived-show search/playback feasibility, discoverable in-thread prompts/help, and same-browser/profile cross-thread Pause controls. Read-only inspection; no production or lifecycle files changed.
